finding.expected: Preserve the strict bounded/non-secret cause surface while making cause identity deterministic across recognized transient path prefixes and retaining enough sanitized bounded Git failure detail for later Human/Brain diagnosis. Normalize or redact recognized subject/diagnostic/basetemp/home path prefixes before deriving persisted fingerprints, and expose only a safely sanitized bounded Git diagnostic excerpt or equivalently discriminating bounded structured Git facts. Keep the 1024-character bound, explicit truncation, no generic stdout/stderr, no environment/credential leakage, no production or existing BP-V4 probe changes, and no semantic root-cause or worker-selection fields.
finding.issue: The diagnostic fingerprints raw exception text and raw Git stderr before path normalization, so fingerprints can vary with randomized diagnostic/basetemp/fixture paths rather than remain stable for the same bounded cause. In addition, Git CalledProcessError observations always persist git_stderr_excerpt as null, leaving only return code plus a raw-stderr fingerprint; for Git-heavy representative failures this is insufficient to distinguish bounded causes such as ref-lock, path, or repository errors that TASK-166 exists to diagnose.
